sections.h2: Which offices do Greenup County owners deal with?
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office collects tax bills, the PVA assesses, and the County Clerk takes over after April 15. All three work out of the Greenup County Courthouse area in the town of Greenup. The Property Valuation Administrator is in Room 209 at 301 Main Street, phone (606) 473-9984, open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Mail to the sheriff goes to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144, and the office answers at (606) 473-9833. The sheriff's tax page lets you pay online with your bill number and mailing address, and online payments carry convenience fees that go to the payment processor, not the sheriff. Refunds and account problems are handled in person at the sheriff's office, not by phone.

  • PVA: values, exemptions and appeals conferences, (606) 473-9984.
  • Sheriff: current-year payment, (606) 473-9833.
  • County Clerk: bills transferred after April 15, (606) 473-7394.
  • County Attorney: questions about the law behind the April 15 transfer, (606) 473-7855.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Greenup County itself?
sections.html:
Greenup County lies along the Ohio River in the northeast corner of Kentucky, and it belongs to the Huntington-Ashland metropolitan area. The General Assembly created it in December 1803 from Mason County. Greenup is the county seat, Flatwoods is the largest city, and the other cities are Bellefonte, Raceland, Russell, South Shore, Worthington and Wurtland.

The river valley is flat and holds most of the industry, shops and housing, while the rest of the county rolls into Appalachian foothills with forest, farms and fishing spots at Greenbo Lake, Tygarts Creek and the Little Sandy River. US 23 follows the river through Russell, Flatwoods, Raceland, Wurtland, Greenup and South Shore and crosses to Portsmouth, Ohio on the U.S. Grant Bridge. The AA Highway, finished in 1995, runs west toward Maysville, and the Industrial Parkway links Wurtland to EastPark and Interstate 64.

Three school systems share the county: Greenup County Schools, Russell Independent and Raceland-Worthington Independent. Census QuickFacts supplies the housing numbers:

  • July 2025 estimate: 35,213 residents, 2.1 percent fewer than the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 80.3 percent.
  • Median owner-occupied home value for 2020 to 2024: $134,000.
  • Median gross rent: $860. Median household income: $60,751. Persons in poverty: 16.7 percent.

sections.h2: What does a Greenup County bill cost after April 15?
sections.html:
It goes from the sheriff to the County Clerk, and the total starts climbing. The sheriff's page says April 15 is the last day to pay at the Sheriff's Office, and that bills turned over to the Clerk pick up fees that the original bill never showed. The sheriff's page cites House Bill 262 as the reason for the April 15 date.

The Department of Revenue prices out the stages for a $1,000 bill. It assumes a 4 percent sheriff commission, so your actual figures depend on the local rate.

Cost of a $1,000 Kentucky tax bill after transfer to the clerk (source: Department of Revenue example)
When paidTotal due
Within 5 business days of transfer$1,387.79
After the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
After a second month of interest (May)$1,627.61
After newspaper advertising (June)$1,659.90
Bought by a third-party purchaser at the sale$1,704.21

Interest runs at 1 percent per month on the certificate. The clerk's sale of delinquent bills must fall 90 to 135 days after the transfer, which in a normal year means July 14 to August 28. Ask the Clerk's office for the third-party purchaser rules if you hold a bill that reaches the sale.

sections.h2: How can a Greenup County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
Start at the PVA, because Kentucky lets only owners who held a conference take a case to the board. The PVA's site explains that every property is revalued each year and physically examined at least once every four years, so a value can move even when your house has not changed.

  • Conferences fall in the May inspection window, which runs 13 days from the first Monday, and staff can meet earlier once notices are mailed.
  • The filing deadline is the close of business the day after inspection ends, at the County Clerk.
  • The board sits four to five weeks later for up to five days, unless the state extends it.
  • Bring documents the board can weigh: building costs, insurance policies, listings and photos. No documents, no reduction.

The PVA's FAQ gives two reminders. Keep your mailing address current with the office, and never treat a missing bill or notice as a reason to skip payment. Rates come from the county, city and school boards, not the PVA.

sections.h2: Does Greenup County have a homestead break?
sections.html:
Owners aged 65 or older, or totally disabled, who live in the house can claim $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026. A house at Greenup County's Census median of $134,000 would be taxed on $84,900.

Bring proof of age to the Greenup County PVA, such as a birth certificate, license or passport. Disability claims need a federal agency or retirement system classification and payments across the full assessment period, renewed annually unless the owner is a service-connected veteran or permanently and totally disabled.

The PVA's FAQ still quotes a saving of about $280 for 2011, so ask the office for the current figure on your own parcel instead of relying on that old estimate.

sections.h2: What should a Greenup County seller settle before closing?
sections.html:
Ask each office for a payoff, because which office holds the bill depends on the date. Before April 15 it sits with the sheriff. Afterward the Clerk has it, and the Clerk's delinquent tax page links the third-party purchaser information and application.

The tax is the owner's personal debt as of January 1, and a delinquent bill's lien can outlast a sale by up to 11 years under KRS 134.420. A buyer's title search will find a lien that has not been released, and a recording and release fee comes with clearing it.

Your closing agent can explain how the current year's bill is divided between you and the buyer. Any bill still open at the Clerk should be paid from your proceeds, and a written payoff from the Clerk shows the full price of clearing the title on a house with several years behind.

faqs.q: Where is Greenup County property tax paid?
faqs.a: At the Greenup County Sheriff's Office through April 15, in person, by mail to PO Box 318, Greenup, KY 41144, or online. Call (606) 473-9833. Processors charge convenience fees on online payments.

faqs.q: Which office explains a Greenup County assessment?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (606) 473-9984, in Room 209 of the courthouse at 301 Main Street. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What changes on April 15 in Greenup County?
faqs.a: The sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the County Clerk. The Clerk adds fees that the original bill did not show, so call (606) 473-7394 for the total.

faqs.q: What is the Greenup County homestead amount?
faqs.a: $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled. At the county median value of $134,000, the taxable amount drops to $84,900.

faqs.q: Will the Greenup County sheriff refund money by phone?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's page says refunds and account corrections must be requested in person at the office, and staff do not process them by phone.
